conversation.content:
Hi there—thank you for making time for this today. I’m Claire, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s a 10-question tool that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally and physically during the past seven days of new motherhood.  

Everything you share is confidential, and our only goal is to make sure you feel heard and supported. We’ll go question by question; each one is quick and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you.  

Whenever you’re ready, we can begin.  

To start: Over the last seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
I’ve still been able to laugh sometimes—like when my husband tried to change a diaper and ended up wearing half of it—but it definitely doesn’t come as easily as it used to.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, I can still laugh here and there—like when my husband tried to change the diaper and got peed on—but it feels like I have to work harder to find the funny side than I did before the baby.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get little sparks of excitement—like when my mom said she’d come hold the baby so I could take a walk—but most of the time it feels pretty flat. I’ll think, “I should be looking forward to coffee with a friend,” and then it just seems like one more thing I have to get through.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Yesterday she wouldn’t settle for her nap and I kept thinking, “I must be doing something wrong—maybe I’m not reading her cues right.” I know babies just cry, but I still feel like it’s my fault when I can’t fix it.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Mostly it’s about her—like I’ll lie awake wondering if her breathing sounds normal or if that tiny rash is something serious. There’s no real reason, but the “what-ifs” just pop in and my heart races until I check the monitor one more time.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Sometimes, yeah—out of nowhere my chest gets tight and I feel like I can’t get a full breath. It’s usually when she’s finally asleep and the house is quiet, which makes no sense, but the sudden “something bad is about to happen” feeling just hits me.
Things have been getting on top of me

A lot of days it feels like I’m barely treading water—like the dishes and laundry and feedings just pile faster than I can handle them. I manage, but by evening I’m exhausted and kind of defeated, wondering how I’ll do it all again tomorrow.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I’ve had a few nights where I lie there feeling heavy and sad—mostly worrying I’m not doing enough for her—and then I can’t drift off even when she’s sleeping. It’s not every night, maybe three or four times this week, but when it happens I just stare at the ceiling until the first morning cries start.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah, I do feel that way some of the time. It’s not all day, but there are moments—especially in the late afternoon when I’m really tired—where I just feel this wave of sadness hit me. I’ll look at her and feel guilty for being sad when she’s healthy and beautiful, but I can’t shake the gloomy feeling.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Not really… I’ve teared up a couple of times, like when she wouldn’t latch and I felt stuck on the couch for an hour, but I haven’t actually cried-cried. It feels like the tears are right there behind my eyes, yet they don’t spill over.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I’ve felt overwhelmed and tired, but hurting myself hasn’t crossed my mind.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 17: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, partner present, infant approx. ≤ 6 wks old (per narrative)

Symptoms / Behavioral Observations
- Diminished pleasure/interest: reports having to “work harder” to laugh; anticipatory enjoyment “flat”  
- Low mood: late-afternoon “waves of sadness,” guilt despite healthy infant  
- Excessive self-blame: attributes infant crying to own competence  
- Anxiety symptoms: intrusive “what-ifs,” nocturnal chest tightness, racing heart, sudden dread  
- Sleep disruption: difficulty initiating sleep 3-4× past week, mood-related rumination  
- Overwhelm: daily tasks accumulating, end-of-day exhaustion, sense of defeat  
- Crying: eyes tearful, no full crying spells; denies self-harm ideation (zero endorsement)

Pattern Summary
Consistent with mixed postpartum anxiety and depressive features; functional impairment (sleep, coping) present; no suicidal/homicidal ideation reported.

Risk Factors Flagged
Moderate: persistent low mood, anhedonia, sleep-mood link, guilt cognitions, situational panic symptoms, subjective impairment.

Safety
Denies thoughts of self-harm; no further safety concerns voiced at screening.

Screening Impression
Elevated scores on core postpartum depression/anxiety domains; requires follow-up with structured diagnostic tool (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) and clinical interview to determine severity and intervention needs.
